clue.text: Tailor swallows last piece of pork kebab

indicators.note: the tailor's word takes another letter down inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a sewer is one who sews, as a tailor does

indicators.note: the final letter of the word pork is the one used

explanation.surface: A tailor at a barbecue gulps down the last bit of pork from a kebab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kebab' looks like the noun at the end of the meal, but here it is a verb: to kebab meat is to spear it.
explanation.definitionFit: To kebab food is to thread it onto a spit, which is exactly what spearing it on a pointed rod does.

clue.text: Writer, man describing Indian cricket tournament

indicators.note: in the sense of drawing around, the chess man encircles the tournament's letters

parts.note: a king is a man, a piece, in chess
the IPL is the Indian Premier League, a Twenty20 cricket competition

explanation.surface: An author is a man reporting on a cricket tournament in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' is used in its geometric sense of drawing round something.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudyard Kipling was the English author of The Jungle Book and Kim.

clue.text: Swore regularly, harbouring anger for snarer of animals

indicators.note: the selected letters shelter the anger word within them
every other letter of swore is taken

parts.note: ire is anger

explanation.surface: Someone cursed at intervals, nursing rage at a trapper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of Swore; 'harbouring' places the anger between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A wirer is one who sets wire snares to catch game such as rabbits.

clue.text: Deny resistance over English dessert one consumed

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece placed over another comes first

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance
pud is British informal for pudding, a dessert
I is the Roman numeral for one
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to admit they ate an English pudding despite opposition.
explanation.definitionFit: To repudiate is to reject or refuse to acknowledge something, close to denying it.

clue.text: Extraordinary individual

definitions.meaning: ... also means single, one only, as in the grammatical number

explanation.surface: A description of a remarkable person: an extraordinary individual.
explanation.definitionFit: Singular means both strikingly unusual and relating to just one separate item or person.

clue.text: Democrat ousting Republican in Jersey is worried

indicators.note: one letter pushes out another and takes its place

parts.note: a jersey is a knitted sweater
R is short for Republican in US politics
D is short for Democrat in US politics

explanation.surface: An American political scene: a Democrat unseats a Republican in New Jersey, which is anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jersey' looks like the US state, but it is the garment.
explanation.definitionFit: To sweat over something is to fret about it, so sweated means worried.

clue.text: Musical composition, revolutionary concept Eno notably has penned

indicators.note: the run of letters turns round and is read backwards
the phrase holds the letters inside it, like a pen enclosing animals

explanation.surface: A groundbreaking musical idea that Brian Eno, the ambient composer, has written down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has penned' hides TENON in 'concepT ENO Notably'; 'revolutionary' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a piece written for nine instruments or voices.

clue.text: Football club accepts member virtually without any checks

indicators.note: the club takes the other piece into itself

parts.note: United is the name of many football clubs, such as Manchester United

indicators.note: almost all of the word is used, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a limb is a member of the body

explanation.surface: A football club signs a player without any background checks, almost.
explanation.definitionFit: Unlimited means without restriction or bounds, so nothing holds it in check.

clue.text: Serve alcohol liberally to school-leaver, for instance

definitions.text: Serve alcohol liberally to school-leaver, for instance

parts.words: Serve alcohol liberally to school-leaver, for instance
parts.note: the twelve letters of 'serve alcohol' freely rearranged give 'school-leaver', an example of this kind of wordplay

explanation.surface: Plying a pupil who has just left school with drink.
explanation.walkthrough: SERVE ALCOHOL and SCHOOL-LEAVER share exactly the same twelve letters; 'liberally' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A word or phrase made by rearranging another's letters is the device itself, so this pair is an example of it.

clue.text: Soldier arranged plan, I hear, to obtain equipment

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper

indicators.note: the letters of plan, I and hear are set in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier organises a plan to get hold of kit, and tells us he has heard so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I hear' looks like a sound signal, but 'hear' is just more anagram fodder alongside 'plan' and 'I'.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraphernalia is the miscellaneous gear and articles needed for an activity, a looser word for kit.

clue.text: Miniaturised secret info from Military Intelligence doctor translated

parts.note: MI is the standard abbreviation, as in MI5 and MI6

indicators.note: the word doctor is turned into a different arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Spy-thriller material: shrunken secret data obtained from an intelligence medic, rendered into another language.
explanation.definitionFit: A microdot is a photograph shrunk to the size of a full stop, a classic espionage method for hiding documents.

clue.text: Sound quality of woodsman's call having delayed echo

indicators.note: one letter of the call comes later than it should, so it is moved further along the word

parts.note: Timber! is the warning shout of a lumberjack as a tree falls
Echo is E in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A lumberjack's shout reverberates with a lagging echo, colouring how it sounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having delayed' moves the E of TIMBER from fifth place to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Timbre is the tonal colour that distinguishes one voice or instrument from another at the same pitch.

clue.text: American ideas oddly ignored gathering information for programme

indicators.note: the outer letters collect another piece inside them, so one goes within the other
the odd-placed letters of ideas are dropped, leaving the even ones

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: An American disregards strange notions while collecting facts for a schedule of business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly ignored' keeps only the even letters of ideas; 'gathering' sets the British slang for information between the American and those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is the list of items to be dealt with at a meeting, a programme of business.

clue.text: Lack of knowledge in school subject undermining Geordie?

indicators.note: in a down clue, the subject goes underneath, so it comes after

parts.note: a Geordie comes from Newcastle in North East England, so NE
science is taught in schools

explanation.surface: A school subject saps the confidence of a Tynesider, leaving him ignorant.
explanation.walkthrough: A Geordie is a native of Newcastle upon Tyne, in the North East of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Nescience is a formal word for ignorance, the absence of knowing.

clue.text: Sad Herb announced period when all working stops

parts.note: down means low in spirits

indicators.note: the herb's name is said out loud, giving a word pronounced the same way

parts.note: thyme is a culinary herb

explanation.surface: A gloomy man called Herb declares that work is halted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Herb' looks like a man's name beside 'Sad', but it is the plant thyme.
explanation.definitionFit: Downtime is time during which a machine or workforce is idle, when no work is done.

clue.text: Employees run into crook few suspect

indicators.note: the run goes inside the jumbled letters
used as an adjective, it marks the letters of crook and few as unreliable, needing rearrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Staff dash into a criminal whom a handful of people suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' looks like a verb, but it is the anagram signal on 'crook few'.
explanation.definitionFit: A workforce is the whole body of people employed by an organisation.

clue.text: Increasing concern primarily about going to Cologne

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word concern is used

parts.note: re means about or concerning
cologne is a scent, a light perfume

explanation.surface: Growing worry about travelling to the German city of Cologne.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cologne' looks like the German city, but here it is eau de cologne, a perfume.
explanation.definitionFit: Crescent as an adjective means growing or waxing, like the moon as it enlarges.

clue.text: Live without normal comforts and basic technology

parts.note: rough means crude or basic
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: Living a simple life with only rudimentary gadgets.
explanation.definitionFit: To rough it is an idiom for living or travelling in uncomfortable, primitive conditions.

clue.text: Wife wearing shades gets sudden pains

indicators.note: the wife has the shades around her, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: tinges are slight shades of colour

explanation.surface: A wife in sunglasses suffers stabs of pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shades' looks like sunglasses, but it means tints of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Twinges are brief, sharp pangs of pain.

clue.text: Frame piece of legislation introduced by socialist

indicators.note: the law comes after the socialist, which introduces it, so it stands second

parts.note: red is a familiar term for a socialist or communist
an act is a law passed by Parliament

explanation.surface: Someone is set up by a law brought in by a left-wing politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frame' looks like a criminal set-up, but it is the sense of drafting or putting into words.
explanation.definitionFit: To redact is to draw up or edit text into a form for publication, as one frames a statement.

clue.text: Stew dog starts to devour, eating rapidly

parts.note: a chow is a Chinese breed of dog

indicators.note: the opening letter of each of the next three words is taken

explanation.surface: A dog begins wolfing down a stew at speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Chowder is a thick soup or stew, typically of seafood.

clue.text: City in revolt claiming this writer's flipping abrasive

indicators.note: the whole assembly is turned over and read backwards
the city and the revolt take the writer's words into their middle

parts.note: EC is the postcode for the City of London
up means risen in rebellion, as in 'the people are up'
the setter refers to himself, so this writer is = I'm

explanation.surface: A rebellious city takes over the setter's work, which he finds infuriatingly harsh.
explanation.walkthrough: EC, IM and UP make ECIMUP; 'flipping' reverses it. 'Flipping' also passes for a mild British curse word.
explanation.definitionFit: Pumice is a light volcanic stone used for scouring and smoothing skin, a natural rubbing agent.

clue.text: Sins of wicked people daughter overlooked

indicators.note: the daughter is left out of the word, so her letter is removed

parts.note: devils are wicked people
D is short for daughter, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: The misdeeds of wicked folk went unnoticed by a daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Evils are wicked acts or wrongdoings, as sins are.

clue.text: Amid disorder Tory departs for tea, perhaps

parts.note: in means amid or among

indicators.note: the party member leaves the larger word, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: confusion is a state of disorder
Con is short for Conservative, the Tory party

explanation.surface: In the chaos, a Conservative politician walks out to go for a cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing CON from CONFUSION leaves FUSION.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea is made by steeping leaves in hot water, the standard example of an infusion.

clue.text: Stocky Greek character's around to protect queen

indicators.note: the turned letters stand guard around the queen, enclosing her
the letters are turned the other way round

parts.note: tau is a Greek letter, and 's (is) adds an S
Q is short for queen, as in chess and cards

explanation.surface: A burly Greek figure is on hand to guard the queen.
explanation.walkthrough: TAUS reversed is SUAT; 'to protect' puts Q after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Squat describes a short, thickset build, as stocky does.

clue.text: Where thin gun possibly is produced?

parts.note: these two words are what the answer's first half makes when the second half is read as an anagram instruction, crushed and rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzle question asking where a slender firearm might be manufactured.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay: HUNTING 'ground' means its letters crushed and rearranged, which can produce THIN GUN; 'possibly' flags that.
explanation.definitionFit: A hunting ground is a place where game is pursued, and so a place where a gun is likely to appear.

clue.text: Those disbelieving stats broadcast about Italy by ambassador

indicators.note: the shuffled statistics go around the other pieces, enclosing them
the letters of stats are scattered into a new order
by means beside, so the ambassador and Italy sit next to each other

parts.note: HE stands for His Excellency, the title of an ambassador
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Sceptics publicise statistics about Italy alongside an ambassador.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' rearranges the statistics word, and 'about' wraps those letters around the ambassador and Italy, splitting them after the second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Atheists are people who do not believe in any god, the archetypal non-believers.

clue.text: Blackmail of former partner wrong?

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: A question: is extorting money from an ex-partner a wrongdoing?
explanation.definitionFit: To extort is to obtain money by threats, which is what a blackmailer does.
